row.team_price_text: From $1.50 to $3.75 per endpoint/mo (published range; quote required)
row.evidence: NinjaOne's docs describe SCIM to automatically create and delete technicians and end users from an IdP (after SAML SSO is set up), while its pricing page says it does not publicly list full pricing and sells per device by quote.
row.notes: Quote-only: NinjaOne (formerly NinjaRMM) publishes no plan table, only a per-endpoint range ($1.50 at 10,000 endpoints to $3.75 at 50 or fewer, varying by region and products) and asks buyers to request a quote; SCIM is documented as a platform identity-provider feature with no plan named. SAML SSO must be configured first. SCIM token expires after six months. Deprovisioning marks users Inactive (still listed). System administrators cannot be assigned via SCIM. Okta OIN app (SAML + SCIM create/update/deactivate/group push); Entra uses a non-gallery app with the generic SCIM endpoint. Per-user fields null because pricing is per device. The Public API 2.0 (OAuth 2.0) can list, create, update and delete technicians and end users and manage role membership.

plans.name: NinjaOne (per-device, quote)
plans.price_text: From $1.50 USD per endpoint/month at 10,000 endpoints to $3.75 USD at 50 or fewer endpoints; full pricing by quote
plans.notes: No public tier table; monthly or annual contracts per the pricing page. SSO/SCIM/API are documented platform features with no plan named.

auth.token_source: Administration → Accounts → Identity Providers → (provider) → Enable SCIM → Generate token

operations.notes: Okta app enables Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users; the activity log lists 'End User Deleted via SCIM' but the docs describe removal as marking users Inactive.

deprovision.data_retained: User marked Inactive and still appears in the users list.

custom.how: NinjaOne extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:ninjaone:2.0:User with organizationId (target organization or 'All') and userType ('endUser' or 'technician')

roles.how: Group mapping in NinjaOne assigns end-user or technician roles to pushed IdP groups; userType attribute picks technician vs end user; system administrator cannot be assigned via SCIM

limitations.text: System administrators cannot be assigned via SCIM, individually or by group.
SCIM-managed users cannot be edited or deleted in NinjaOne unless SCIM is temporarily deactivated.
Okta Import Users and Import Profile Updates are not supported.
SCIM secret token expires six months after generation and must be replaced in the IdP.

scim.notes: The SCIM tenant URL is shown in NinjaOne (Administration → Accounts → Identity Providers) per IdP; its pattern is not published. Version 2.0 inferred from the urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:ninjaone:2.0 schema URN.

audit_log_api.notes: GET /v2/activities returns the activity log; SCIM and SSO events are logged as SSO-type activities.

user_api.notes: Base host is the customer's regional instance (e.g. app.ninjarmm.com); the /v2 paths are from the published OpenAPI document.

okta.notes: OIN 'NinjaOne' (last updated Aug. 21 2025) ticks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate and Group Push (read from page markup).

entra.notes: Vendor guide uses a non-gallery Entra enterprise app with the NinjaOne SCIM tenant URL and token.

google.notes: Custom SAML app; vendor says it has not tested Google Workspace SAML.

onelogin.notes: Vendor guide points to the 'NinjaRMM' app in the OneLogin catalogue for SAML; no provisioning documented. OneLogin connector page not loaded.

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud guide covers SAML SSO only.

fallbacks.notes: CSV import covers end users per organization; technicians are created individually.

open_questions: No NinjaOne page states whether SCIM/SSO are included for every customer or tied to particular products or contract terms (quote-only).
SCIM base URL pattern, filtering, pagination and rate limits are not published.
Whether SCIM deactivation frees a licence or ends sessions is not documented (licensing is per device, not per user).
Whether SCIM DELETE hard-deletes users is unclear: the activity log lists 'End User Deleted via SCIM' while the guide says removed users are marked Inactive.
